name: Cytochrome P450 1A1
function: Bioactivation of polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and heterocyclic amines
notes: AhR-inducible; primary carcinogen activator in smokers

name: Cytochrome P450 1A2
function: Metabolism of caffeine, theophylline, acetaminophen, and aromatic amines
notes: ~13% of hepatic P450 content; significant in aromatic amine carcinogenesis

name: Cytochrome P450 1B1
function: Catechol estrogen synthesis; PAH bioactivation in extrahepatic tissues
notes: Associated with congenital glaucoma; overexpressed in many cancers

name: Cytochrome P450 2A6
function: Nicotine and coumarin 7-hydroxylation; nitrosamine activation
notes: Major nicotine-metabolizing enzyme; CYP2A6*4 deletion in East Asians

name: Cytochrome P450 2A7
function: No established catalytic activity; pseudogene-related
notes: Closely related to CYP2A6 but lacks known catalytic activity

name: Cytochrome P450 2A13
function: Bioactivation of tobacco-specific nitrosamines in lung
notes: Lung-selective NNK activator; implicated in lung cancer from tobacco

name: Cytochrome P450 2B6
function: Metabolism of efavirenz, cyclophosphamide, bupropion, and ketamine
notes: Highly polymorphic (~30% of individuals are poor metabolizers); CYP2B6*6 most common variant

name: Cytochrome P450 2C8
function: Metabolism of paclitaxel, thiazolidinediones, amodiaquine, and repaglinide
notes: ~7% hepatic P450; gemfibrozil inhibition causes repaglinide DDIs

name: Cytochrome P450 2C9
function: Metabolism of warfarin, phenytoin, NSAIDs, and losartan
notes: ~18% hepatic P450; CYP2C9*2 and *3 cause warfarin sensitivity; critical for anticoagulation dosing

name: Cytochrome P450 2C18
function: Limited known substrate list; shares substrates with CYP2C9 at low capacity
notes: Low hepatic expression; predominant in skin

name: Cytochrome P450 2C19
function: Metabolism of proton pump inhibitors, clopidogrel activation, and antidepressants
notes: CYP2C19*2 and *17; clopidogrel requires CYP2C19 activation — poor metabolizers have increased stroke risk

name: Cytochrome P450 2D6
function: Metabolism of codeine, tamoxifen, haloperidol, and many antidepressants
notes: ~25% of drugs; ~7% Caucasians are poor metabolizers; codeine fatalities in ultra-rapid metabolizers

name: Cytochrome P450 2E1
function: Oxidation of ethanol, acetaminophen, and small organic molecules; ROS generation
notes: Activated by ethanol and fasting; major source of ROS in alcoholic liver disease

name: Cytochrome P450 2F1
function: Bioactivation of 3-methylindole and naphthalene in lung
notes: Lung-specific; contributes to pneumotoxicity of 3-methylindole (skatole)

name: Cytochrome P450 2J2
function: Epoxygenation of arachidonic acid; cardioprotective EET synthesis
notes: Major cardiac P450; EETs (products) are vasodilatory and cardioprotective

name: Cytochrome P450 2R1
function: Vitamin D 25-hydroxylation (first activation step)
notes: CYP2R1 mutations cause vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1B

name: Cytochrome P450 2S1
function: Metabolism of retinoids and inflammatory lipid mediators
notes: AhR-inducible; expressed in tissues exposed to environmental agents

name: Cytochrome P450 2U1
function: ω-Hydroxylation of arachidonic acid and endocannabinoids
notes: Mutations cause hereditary spastic paraplegia (SPG56)

name: Cytochrome P450 2W1
function: Bioactivation of pro-drugs in colon cancer cells
notes: Expressed in colon tumors but not normal colon; target for cancer prodrug activation

name: Cytochrome P450 3A4
function: Metabolism of >50% of clinically used drugs; extremely broad substrate range
notes: ~40% hepatic P450; largest active site cavity (~1385 Å³); peripheral allosteric site; rifampin induction

name: Cytochrome P450 3A5
function: Overlaps CYP3A4 substrates; important in kidney and ethnic populations
notes: CYP3A5*3 expressor frequency varies greatly by ethnicity; critical for tacrolimus dosing in transplant

name: Cytochrome P450 3A7
function: Fetal-predominant isoform; DHEA-S hydroxylation in placenta
notes: Predominant CYP3A in fetal liver; replaced by CYP3A4 postnatally

name: Cytochrome P450 3A43
function: Very low hepatic expression; testosterone 6β-hydroxylation at minimal capacity
notes: Lowest expressed CYP3A isoform; physiological role unclear

name: Cytochrome P450 4A11
function: ω-Hydroxylation of fatty acids; 20-HETE synthesis important in blood pressure regulation
notes: 20-HETE is a vasoconstrictor; CYP4A11 variants linked to hypertension

name: Cytochrome P450 4A22
function: Very low catalytic activity; may be a pseudogene in some individuals
notes: Incomplete coding sequence in many haplotypes

name: Cytochrome P450 4B1
function: ω-Hydroxylation of valproic acid and medium-chain fatty acids; pneumotoxicant activation
notes: Human orthologue has lower activity than rabbit CYP4B1 due to Pro at position 427

name: Cytochrome P450 4F2
function: Leukotriene B4 ω-hydroxylation; vitamin K and vitamin E metabolism
notes: CYP4F2*3 (V433M) reduces vitamin K metabolism; warfarin dose requirement affected

name: Cytochrome P450 4F3
function: Leukotriene B4 ω-hydroxylation in neutrophils; inflammatory lipid inactivation
notes: Two splice variants: CYP4F3A (neutrophils) and CYP4F3B (liver)

name: Cytochrome P450 4F8
function: ω-2 hydroxylation of prostaglandins H1 and H2
notes: Highly expressed in seminal vesicles; role in reproductive biology

name: Cytochrome P450 4F11
function: ω-Hydroxylation of fatty acids and vitamin K; overlaps with CYP4F2
notes: Overlapping activity with CYP4F2 in vitamin K metabolism

name: Cytochrome P450 4F12
function: ω-Hydroxylation of arachidonic acid; some xenobiotic metabolism
notes: Intestinal expression suggests role in first-pass metabolism

name: Cytochrome P450 4F22
function: ω-Hydroxylation of ultra-long-chain fatty acids in skin barrier
notes: Mutations cause autosomal recessive congenital ichthyosis (ARCI)

name: Cytochrome P450 4V2
function: Fatty acid ω-hydroxylation in retina; vitamin D3 side-chain hydroxylation
notes: Mutations cause Bietti crystalline corneoretinal dystrophy

name: Cytochrome P450 4X1
function: Anandamide and arachidonic acid hydroxylation in brain
notes: Expressed in brain vasculature; possible role in neurological homeostasis

name: Cytochrome P450 4Z1
function: Arachidonic acid metabolism in mammary gland; overexpressed in breast cancer
notes: Breast cancer biomarker candidate; promotes angiogenesis via EETs

name: Cytochrome P450 5A1 (Thromboxane Synthase)
function: Converts prostaglandin H2 to thromboxane A2; platelet aggregation and vasoconstriction
notes: Not a monooxygenase but classified as CYP; TXA2 is the target of aspirin's antiplatelet effect upstream

name: Cytochrome P450 7A1
function: Cholesterol 7α-hydroxylation; rate-limiting step in bile acid synthesis (classic pathway)
notes: CYP7A1 mutations cause hypercholesterolemia; regulated by FXR and LXR

name: Cytochrome P450 7B1
function: 7α-Hydroxylation of oxysterols and neurosteroids (DHEA, pregnenolone)
notes: CYP7B1 mutations cause spastic paraplegia type 5 (SPG5) and neonatal liver failure

name: Cytochrome P450 8A1 (Prostacyclin Synthase)
function: Converts prostaglandin H2 to prostacyclin (PGI2); vasodilation and platelet inhibition
notes: Balance between TXA2 (CYP5A1) and PGI2 (CYP8A1) determines thrombotic risk

name: Cytochrome P450 8B1
function: Sterol 12α-hydroxylation; determines cholic acid vs. chenodeoxycholic acid ratio in bile
notes: Regulates hydrophobicity of bile acid pool; insulin-regulated

name: Cytochrome P450 11A1 (Cholesterol Side-chain Cleavage)
function: Catalyzes three sequential reactions converting cholesterol to pregnenolone (rate-limiting in steroidogenesis)
notes: Mitochondrial; STAR protein delivers cholesterol; mutations cause congenital adrenal lipoid hyperplasia

name: Cytochrome P450 11B1
function: 11β-Hydroxylation of 11-deoxycortisol to cortisol
notes: Mutations cause congenital adrenal hyperplasia (form 2); ACTH-regulated

name: Cytochrome P450 11B2 (Aldosterone Synthase)
function: Three-step conversion of deoxycorticosterone to aldosterone (11β-hydroxylation, 18-hydroxylation, 18-oxidation)
notes: Target for primary hyperaldosteronism treatment; CYP11B1/B2 chimeras cause familial hyperaldosteronism type I

name: Cytochrome P450 17A1
function: Bifunctional: 17α-hydroxylase (glucocorticoid pathway) and 17,20-lyase (androgen/estrogen pathway)
notes: Abiraterone (Zytiga) targets CYP17A1 in castration-resistant prostate cancer; cytochrome b5 activates lyase activity

name: Cytochrome P450 19A1 (Aromatase)
function: Aromatization of androgens to estrogens (testosterone → estradiol; androstenedione → estrone)
notes: Primary target in hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer; exemestane is a suicide inhibitor

name: Cytochrome P450 20A1
function: Orphan P450; no established substrates identified
notes: Expressed in brain; true physiological substrates unknown

name: Cytochrome P450 21A2
function: 21-Hydroxylation of progesterone and 17α-hydroxyprogesterone in cortisol and aldosterone synthesis
notes: Most common cause of congenital adrenal hyperplasia (>90% of cases); gene duplication/pseudogene CYP21A1P

name: Cytochrome P450 24A1
function: Sequential 24- and 23-hydroxylation of 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3; vitamin D catabolism
notes: Vitamin D-induced; mutations cause infantile hypercalcemia (IIH)

name: Cytochrome P450 26A1
function: Retinoic acid 4-hydroxylation; controls retinoic acid tissue levels
notes: RA-inducible; essential for establishing RA gradients in embryogenesis

name: Cytochrome P450 26B1
function: Retinoic acid 4-hydroxylation in extrahepatic tissues and embryo
notes: Mutations cause craniosynostosis with vertebral and sternal fusion

name: Cytochrome P450 26C1
function: Metabolism of all-trans and 9-cis retinoic acid
notes: Expressed during embryogenesis; cooperates with CYP26A1 in RA clearance

name: Cytochrome P450 27A1
function: Sterol 27-hydroxylation in bile acid synthesis; 25-hydroxylation of vitamin D
notes: Mutations cause cerebrotendinous xanthomatosis (CTX); mitochondrial

name: Cytochrome P450 27B1 (1α-Hydroxylase)
function: 1α-Hydroxylation of 25-hydroxyvitamin D3 to the active form 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D3
notes: Mutations cause vitamin D-dependent rickets type 1A (VDDR1A)

name: Cytochrome P450 27C1
function: Retinoid 3,4-desaturase; converts vitamin A1 to A2 (3-dehydroretinol) in retina
notes: Shifts visual pigment peak absorbance in fish; role in human retina being characterized

name: Cytochrome P450 39A1
function: 7α-Hydroxylation of 24S-hydroxycholesterol; oxysterol metabolism
notes: Links brain cholesterol metabolism (via CYP46A1) to hepatic bile acid synthesis

name: Cytochrome P450 46A1
function: Cholesterol 24S-hydroxylation; predominant pathway for brain cholesterol turnover
notes: 24S-OHC crosses blood-brain barrier; CYP46A1 variants linked to Alzheimer's disease risk

name: Cytochrome P450 51A1 (Lanosterol 14α-Demethylase)
function: 14α-Demethylation of lanosterol and dihydrolanosterol in cholesterol biosynthesis
notes: Evolutionarily most conserved CYP; azole antifungals target fungal CYP51 (Erg11); human off-target inhibition causes DDIs
